judged_text: The added block performs an eager, unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation — not gated on token expiry and not routed through refreshOAuthTokens — and any failure (non-OK status, network error, schema mismatch) rejects the connection promise. Every Salesforce calendar operation now pays an extra OAuth round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a DB write, and operations that previously succeeded with the stored access token now hard-fail at construction time whenever the refresh endpoint hiccups, turning a lazy refresh into a per-operation outage.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` immediately after `const credentialKey = credential.key ...` and before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no expiry check or conditional gating, no use of the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, and the code throws/rejects on non-"OK" statusText and on schema/parse failure (and also performs a `prisma.credential.update` every time this path runs). This means the service can now fail to construct even if the previously stored access token would still work, and it introduces an extra OAuth call + DB write on each construction/path execution.
